captions.linkedin:
Stop screening on net earnings. You're sorting on noise. 📊

Net income gets distorted by R&D timing, SG&A choices, write-downs, tax tricks, and one-time charges. By the time it hits the bottom line, the signal is buried.

Novy-Marx (Journal of Financial Economics, 2013, Fama-DFA Prize winner) showed that gross profit to assets is the cleaner profitability signal. And it predicts cross-sectional stock returns as powerfully as book-to-market value.

The complete logic:

🔹 SIGNAL. Gross profit divided by total assets. That's it. No earnings games, no accruals manipulation.
🔹 RANK every US stock by the ratio. Decile sort.
🔹 LONG the top decile, SHORT the bottom decile. Value-weighted.
🔹 REBALANCE annually in June (the Fama-French timing convention).
🔹 Combine with value: the two factors are negatively correlated, so the joint Sharpe is higher than value alone.

Why it works: profitable firms reinvest earnings into compounding businesses. Unprofitable firms burn capital. The market underweights this because it screens on noisier earnings metrics.

Novy-Marx replicated the effect internationally. It's foundational to the Fama-French 5-factor model.
